notes:
The Michael Brailove Photographic Negatives read whole — 51 records, one 1964 assignment in the Western Addition made for the neighbourhood's own block clubs. 29 records give no street number and are skipped: block-club meetings, voter registration tables, street corners, children in doorways. 22 addressed records fold into 7 findings over 7 distinct addresses.

**Nothing was published, and the reason is the subject.** Four of the seven addresses are gone from EAS outright — 1884 Sutter Street, 1109 Golden Gate Avenue, 1832 Fillmore Street (Freedom House) and 1745 Fillmore Street (the Temple Theater). The other three resolve, and resolving is the trap: 914 McAllister Street now sits on a 1973 block the assessor files as 1049 Golden Gate Avenue and which carries 900 through 950 McAllister on one lot; 878 McAllister on a 1974 block filed as 735 Gough Street; 949 Fillmore Street on a building the roll dates 1975. Brailove photographed these blocks the year before the A-2 clearances reached them, and the city reissued the numbers on what replaced them.

So all three resolutions were declined and the whole collection is recorded here rather than on a page. That is the honest yield of a photograph collection of a neighbourhood that was demolished, and the findings file is the only place these buildings are now indexed by number and date.

coverage.note: Read every record in the collection: 51 unique catalogue records, 22 of which give a street number, folding into 7 findings over 7 distinct addresses. 3 resolved and all 3 declined — the parcels carry 1973–1975 redevelopment buildings, not the 1964 ones photographed. 4 unresolved: the addresses are gone from EAS. Nothing published.
